purpose: Do not reintroduce 200 quotation fragments without passage-level source review; distinguish contextual excerpts, punctuation/orthography changes, traditional typology and actual source text.
sourceCorpusEdition: Inherited donor labelled Douay–Rheims, compared against Douay–Rheims (Challoner) Wikisource witness; Crampon 1923 separately linked.
rules: No source link alone certifies an excerpt or grants reproduction rights.
English comparison is not bilingual certification; exact Crampon verse collation and edition rights remain pending.
Preserve all 200 IDs, mystery and bead ownership; the production player may not use the historical fragments.
Typology in the Assumption and Coronation must never be styled as direct Gospel narrative.
Psalm, Canticles, Judith and Isaias references need canonical-edition mapping; never guess Psalm numbering.
Automatic triage flags are review prompts, not a declaration of error or theological approval.

primaryWitnessReview.explanation: Accurate core salutation; verse 28 begins with the angel's arrival and attribution, missing from the inherited excerpt.
The Magnificat words are biblical, but Luke 1:46 identifies Mary as speaker before the selected extract.
Luke 2:7 uses firstborn and has differing punctuation/commas in the inspected Challoner witness.
Luke 2:35 adds punctuation around 'many hearts' that the donor drops.
Luke 2:46 opens 'And it came to pass, that,' and uses commas absent in this abridgement.
Matthew 3:15 includes Jesus' speaker introduction and reads 'fulfill' in the inspected Challoner witness, rather than the donor's 'fulfil'.
John 2:5 is a complete intelligible verse in the inspected English witness.
Matthew 6:33 is a complete intelligible verse in the inspected English witness.
Matthew 17:2 is a complete intelligible verse in the inspected English witness.
Matthew 26:26 is abbreviated to Christ's words, without the breaking of bread and narrative attribution.
Matthew 26:39 is abbreviated and the 'Nevertheless' punctuation does not reproduce the inspected witness.
John 19:1 changes the commas surrounding Pilate and Jesus; not an exact-source transcription.
Matthew 27:30 drops a comma after 'reed' in the inspected edition.
Luke 23:28 omits Jesus' introductory speech attribution.
John 19:30 omits the sentence identifying Jesus as speaker after taking the vinegar.
John 20:1 starts with 'And on the first day of the week'; the donor begins after this temporal context.
Acts 1:9 is a complete intelligible verse in the inspected English witness.
Acts 2:4 uses commas in the inspected verse; the donor places a colon after 'Holy Ghost'.
Psalm 131:8 is cited in the Vulgate-based devotional tradition; verify verse mapping to each target Bible. Ark typology does not directly narrate the Assumption.
Revelation/Apocalypse 12:1 is an image of the Woman, not a narrative of Mary's historical coronation; the donor omits the opening 'And a great sign appeared in heaven'.
